source.title: Mean-field Behaviour of Neural Tangent Kernel for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Soufiane Hayou; A. Doucet; J. Rousseau

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The title in the supplied metadata differs from the paper title in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares initialization schemes, depths, and training methods and reports classification accuracy, bearing on practical trainability. It does not measure training classification error directly or test most of the claim versions' specific outcomes.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test accuracy, not training classification error; it cannot establish near-zero training error. Table 3 compares scaled and standard ResNet test accuracy, not the claim's training-error outcome. The learning-rate plot reports accuracy, while the passband's numeric values are figure-only. Citations to other studies are not results from this paper.
record.test_reason: The SGD experiments test V4's trainable-depth component: plain FFNNs and CNNs learn at depths 30 and 300 with activation-matched EOC initialization, whereas Ordered initialization gives approximately chance test accuracy. They do not establish training speed or test V5's above-threshold recovery dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that the infinite-width-then-infinite-depth NTK regime becomes trivial, with initialization controlling its convergence rate, and cannot fully explain deep networks trained with SGD. Their experiments show initialization-dependent nontrivial learning in deep plain networks, and their NTK analysis motivates a learning-rate passband.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes infinite-width NTK dynamics and compares NTK training with parameter-space SGD; the claim concerns training error and other studies' specific recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, initialization scheme (EOC versus Ordered), architecture, training method, and learning rate affect the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual networks learn under both EOC and Ordered initialization; the recorded outcomes are test accuracies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual architectures can reduce dependence of successful classification learning on the tested initialization variances.

fits_no_version.finding: The upper learning-rate passband boundary scales approximately as inverse depth; its lower boundary is nearly unrelated to depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested Fashion-MNIST ReLU FFNNs, the learning-rate interval permitting learning has a depth-dependent upper boundary.

record.problems: The classification experiments report test accuracy rather than training error. The learning-rate plot is figure-only in the supplied text, and the study does not report stability thresholds or loss trajectories for the claimed above-threshold recovery.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 includes NTK-training results, but these are not parameter-space gradient training outcomes named by V4. MNIST results and Table 3 CIFAR100 scaled-versus-standard ResNet test accuracies do not test a listed version's stated training-error outcome and were left out.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the special-initialization and Fixup components.

Direct training-speed comparisons; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization; training 10,000-layer plain CNNs. Reported classification outcomes establish nontrivial learning, not near-zero training error.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, transient loss increases and curvature drops, sharpness hovering at the threshold, and divergence despite starting below it.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

missing.what: Add six Ordered-initialization SGD controls: FFNN-ReLU, FFNN-Tanh, and CNN-ReLU at depths 30 and 300 on CIFAR-10. Each dash denotes approximately 10% test accuracy, rather than an unavailable measurement. These are the essential controls for R9–R11 and R13–R15.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. Remove both extracted limits_scope verdicts: lower test accuracy at depth 300 does not negate the observed EOC benefit, and unmeasured V5 dynamics are untested. MNIST results bearing on V4 were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports test accuracy rather than training classification error and does not test corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
No two-layer teacher-student experiment or student-width sweep is reported.
The paper compares architectures and depths using test accuracy, but does not report plain-network training error versus depth or a paired identity-shortcut comparison on training error.

The paper compares EOC and ordered initialization for FFNN, CNN, and ResNet at selected depths using test accuracy. It does not test orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization or 10,000-layer plain CNN training.

The paper reports a learning-rate/depth accuracy sweep for FFNNs on Fashion-MNIST and describes an upper passband bound. It does not test recovery above a stability threshold, the catapult loss trajectory, or sharpness hovering at a threshold.
